react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm analysis of ten differentially abundant metabolites reveals a dominant, multi-method consensus centred on steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned WP:WP496 'Steroid biosynthesis' as the top-ranked pathway (FDR 1.0×10⁻¹⁵, fold-enrichment 2502×) with five input steroids as hits (DHEA, androstenedione, estrone, testosterone, dihydrotestosterone), representing a 41.7% overlap with the 12-member canonical pathway. The same five steroids drove simultaneous enrichment in 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' (KEGG:map00150 / SMPDB:SMP00068, FDR 2.9×10⁻¹⁴) and 'Metabolism of steroid hormones' (REACT:R-HSA-196071, FDR 1.8×10⁻¹³). Independent m/z-direct activity analysis via mummichog confirmed two KEGG-derived steroid networks as the top hits: 'C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism' (p=0.000504, 13/13 metabolites overlapped) and 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' (p=0.000672, 12/12 metabolites overlapped). MetaboAnalystR KEGG ORA identified hsa00140 (steroid pathway) as the sole return. The five driver steroids are structurally non-conflicting (unique InChIKey first-blocks confirmed by reconciliation) and collectively define a convergent signal spanning de novo steroid anabolism through androgen/estrogen interconversion. The non-steroid metabolites (coumarin, spironolactone, 3-hydroxy-L-proline, pyrocatechol, doxycycline) do not contribute to the top steroid hits; coumarin appears only in a secondary xenobiotics metabolism hit (p=0.035) via mummichog. The biological story is one of systemic perturbation of the C21 steroid axis — encompassing androgen precursors (DHEA, androstenedione), active androgens (testosterone, dihydrotestosterone), and the oestrogen precursor estrone — consistent with a treatment that either inhibits steroidogenic enzymes or displaces steroid ligands at receptor level.
